messages:
Diego Ramos: Hi all  first day and unpacking the Surface. Tried to join Azure AD during OOBE but it errors out with 'TPM attestation failed' and Intune enrollment never completes. BitLocker says 'recovery needed' (no key shown). Anyone run into this with company Surfaces?
Anya Singh (IT): welcome Diego! can you share the serial? TPM attestation fails usually when the device firmware needs an owner reset or TPM needs to be cleared. serial?
Diego Ramos: serial PF2-7G4-9K2. I bought it from the company portal ship-to-me flow.
mdm-bot: Device PF27G49K2: provisioning ticket created. Intune enrollment: failed (TPM error). BitLocker status: recovery required.
Anya Singh (IT): thanks. I'm seeing the device in Autopilot but the attestation cert didn't complete. two quick options: 1) if you have any data on the device, backup then we can clear TPM via UEFI and re-run OOBE; 2) if you want to keep current state, we can escalate to hardware team to fetch attestation from MSFT portal. Which do you prefer?
Diego Ramos: prefer to avoid wiping if possible  I have a few files on Desktop but nothing critical. do we have a recovery key anywhere?
it-ops-bot: Policy: BitLocker keys for company devices are escrowed to Azure AD upon successful device join. If attestation failed pre-join, key may not be escrowed. Ticket template: "Surface TPM attestation failure for <serial>".
Diego Ramos: ok opened ticket IT-2201: "Surface TPM attestation failure for PF27G49K2". linked serial and added note about files.
Anya Singh (IT): received IT-2201. I'll pull the device logs remotely and try a soft-fix first (toggle TPM ownership via UEFI without full wipe). Can you boot into UEFI and check Windows Security -> Device Security -> Security processor details?
Diego Ramos: in Windows Security it says "Security processor: TPM not ready" and under Diagnostics it recommends clearing. There's also an option in UEFI for "Clear security processor". Should I proceed?
Anya Singh (IT): hold onI'll remote into the device in a sec. clearing TPM without MDM guidance can cause BitLocker recovery. If we clear, we'll need to create a temporary key backup first.
Leo Park: tagging in from Hardware ops  if the attestation cert is missing we can request a manual attestation from MSFT but it adds 1-2 business days. If the user is OK, clearing TPM and re-running Autopilot is quicker.
Diego Ramos: I'm fine with a short outage, prefer faster path.
Anya Singh (IT): ok. I'm going to push a one-time local admin token and a tiny script to back up the BitLocker protector to a USB (encrypted) so you won't lose files. Creating ticket for admin: "Temporary local admin 24h for PF27G49K2".
mdm-bot: Temporary admin token issued: admin-24h-7b2a.
Diego Ramos: got the admin token popup, created admin user, running the script now.
Anya Singh (IT): nice. script completed and exported recovery key to encrypted USB. now clearing TPM in UEFI and re-running OOBE. you'll be offline for a few minutes.
Diego Ramos: booting to UEFI and doing clearok cleared, re-running OOBE.
mdm-bot: Autopilot enrollment retried for PF27G49K2. Intune enrollment in progress.
Diego Ramos: joining Azure AD now  it worked! Intune shows device as 'Enrolled' and BitLocker started encrypting automatically. recovery key uploaded to Azure AD (I can see part of the key via portal).
Anya Singh (IT): great. I'll remove the temporary admin after you confirm Docker and VPN install. remember to eject the USB with the exported key (we'll delete the copy after verification).
Diego Ramos: Docker Desktop installer wants a privileged helper and Windows features (Hyper-V) enabled. I don't have admin to enable Hyper-V. Do we usually grant admin for this?
it-ops-bot: New-hires policy: Temporary admin for dev tooling available on request. Template: "Temporary admin for <serial> for dev tooling". Default duration 48h.
Diego Ramos: opened IT-2202: "Temporary admin for PF27G49K2 for Docker & VPN install".
Anya Singh (IT): approved IT-2202 for 48h. admin rights applied, should take effect after elevation prompt.
Diego Ramos: elevation prompt appeared, enabling Hyper-V now and installing Docker. VPN client installed and connected. BitLocker shows 4% encrypting (just started).
Anya Singh (IT): all good. a few notes: keep the device plugged in for faster encryption; we'll automatically revoke admin after 48h; the exported recovery key on USB will be deleted from our staging server in 24h. If anything weird pops up, ping me directly.
Diego Ramos: thank you so much! also Leo, thanks for the quick hardware guidance.
Leo Park: glad it worked out. welcome aboard Diego! ping me if you want the quick Surface tips doc.
Diego Ramos: will do, thanks everyone :smile:
